samples.summary: Markdown export silently replaces every backend-hosted (relative-URL) image with the `[image]` placeholder
samples.evidence: `isSafeImageSrc()` (markdown.ts:284-290) accepts only `data:image/...;base64,...` or a string `isSafeUrl()` accepts, and `isSafeUrl` does `new URL(href)` with no base — so it returns false for any relative URL (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31, and packages/core/test/url.test.ts:20 asserts `isSafeUrl('example.com') === false`). Docs image sources are routinely relative: `docsImageUploader` returns `resolveImageUrl(url)` and `resolveImageUrl` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18) returns the backend's `/images/<id>` unchanged whenever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is empty (a same-origin deployment). Every such image therefore serializes to `[image]` in the new `.md` export (and in the CLI's `docs content --format md`), losing all pictures from the document the export exists to produce. The same rule drops relative `href`s (markdown.ts:224) to plain text — DOCX/HTML-imported links are the realistic source. The new tests only cover absolute and malicious URLs, so nothing catches this.

samples.summary: Case-sensitive `startsWith('data:')` lets an uppercase `DATA:` image URI bypass the `inlineImages=false` placeholder while the new allowlist regex accepts it case-insensitively
samples.evidence: `const isDataUri = image.src.startsWith('data:')` (line 297) is case-sensitive, but `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` is `/^data:image\/...$/i` (line 280-281). For `src = 'Data:image/png;base64,AAAA'`, the `!opts.inlineImages` placeholder branch is skipped (isDataUri === false), then `isSafeImageSrc` matches the case-insensitive regex, so the full base64 payload is emitted into terminal output / the CLI's default `--inline-images=false` mode — exactly the case the placeholder exists to prevent. The two checks should use the same case rule.

samples.summary: Dialog validates only the margins, so a non-finite/non-positive paper size lets `setPageSetup` throw RangeError out of the submit handler
samples.evidence: The `error` computation (lines 142-149) checks the margin strings and the margin sums against `pageWidth`/`pageHeight`, but never checks that `paperSize.width`/`height` are finite and positive. `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:~963) throws `RangeError` for exactly that case. A DOCX import can produce such a size: `parsePageSetup` does `Math.round(twipsToPx(parseInt(w, 10)))` on the raw `w:pgSz/@w` attribute (packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts:300-301), which yields `NaN` for a malformed attribute and is stored as a `Custom` paper size. With `pageWidth = NaN` every `>=` comparison is false, so no error is shown, Apply stays enabled, and clicking it throws an uncaught exception from a React event handler: nothing is applied, the dialog stays open, and the user gets no feedback.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition` applies `+1` to an un-normalized endpoint for table cell-range selections, so the painter can copy the format from the wrong cell
samples.evidence: `formatSourcePosition()` (text-editor.ts:402-410) assumes `getNormalizedRange()` orders the endpoints, but for a cell-rectangle selection `normalizeRange` returns `{ start: range.anchor, end: range.focus }` verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:120-128) — no ordering at all. For a cell drag started at the bottom-right cell, `normalized.start` is the anchor in that cell, so `copyFormat()` reads the format from the last cell of the rectangle (and at `anchor.offset + 1`, an offset that has no relation to the highlighted content), which is the same class of bug the `+1`/normalization was introduced to fix for text selections.

samples.summary: Page Setup opened from a Radix `DropdownMenuItem` via `onClick` may be unusable on mobile (menu-close/dialog-open race)
samples.evidence: The mobile overflow entry uses `<DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setPageSetupOpen(true)}>`. Radix closes the menu on select and restores focus / clears its `pointer-events: none` body lock asynchronously; opening a Dialog in the same tick commonly leaves the dialog non-interactive or immediately dismissed. The other menu-driven surfaces in this file defer commits to `onCloseAutoFocus` for the analogous reason (see the `slimAlign` comment at line ~358). No test exercises the mobile path (`useIsMobile()` is stubbed to false in both new test files), so this is unverified either way.

samples.summary: `parseInches` rejects the very partial input its comment says it protects
samples.evidence: The `MarginDraft` doc comment says margins are kept as raw strings "so a half-typed \"0.\" is not clobbered", but `/^\d*\.?\d+$/` (line 79) requires at least one digit after the dot, so `"0."` parses to `null` and the dialog shows the "Margins must be zero or a positive number" alert and disables Apply while the user is mid-typing. (Also rejects `"+1"`, `"1e0"`.) Cosmetic, but the comment and the code disagree.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: isSafeImageSrc (markdown.ts:284-290) accepts only a data:image/... base64 URI or a string isSafeUrl() approves, and isSafeUrl (core/src/url/index.ts:24-31) parses with `new URL(href)` and no base, returning false for any relative URL (its own docstring says so). A failing src therefore yields the '[image]' placeholder (markdown.ts:305-307), and a failing href degrades to plain text (markdown.ts:224). Relative srcs are a real shape in this model, not hypothetical: the backend returns `/images/<key>` (backend/src/image/image.service.ts:128), frontend resolveImageUrl returns it unchanged when VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is empty (frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:5,16 — `?? ""` then `if (!BACKEND_BASE) return url`), and both the CLI image fetcher (cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:26-30) and the PDF image painter (docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:58-63) explicitly document handling server-relative `/images/<id>` sources — i.e. the other exporters resolve them while the Markdown serializer drops them. No upstream guard resolves the src first: frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44 and cli/src/docs/content.ts:129 both hand the untouched Document to serializeMarkdown. Tests (docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts:539-555) cover only absolute/malicious schemes for images, so nothing catches it. That is silent data loss in the export path — a correctness defect; no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.
